    03 / What the strip cannot tell you

    Contiguous is a description.
    Free is an interpretation.

    A long leisure stretch can include responsibility for a child. A switch from reading to music may be a choice. An unreported interruption leaves no mark at all.

    The diary measures a sequence of reported main activities. Its shape matters. It is still not a measure of who owns the time.

    Definitions, boundaries and missing time

    Default leisure includes all six-digit activity codes beginning 12 (socializing, relaxing and leisure) or 13 (sports, exercise and recreation), including their waiting categories. This is an explicit analytical definition, not the exact BLS published “leisure and sports” aggregate. “Include leisure travel” adds 1812xx and 1813xx. “Include social phone calls” adds 160101 and 160102. Religious activities, caregiving and eating remain separate. These activities can also be meaningful or enjoyable; the categories do not judge their value.

    By default, consecutive included episodes form one stretch, even if their activity codes differ. The split option starts a new stretch when the six-digit code changes; repeated adjacent episodes of the same code still join. It is a coding sensitivity test, not a count of interruptions. The longest stretch is the largest sum of contiguous included minutes. No gaps are bridged, and midnight does not create a break.

    The recorded day runs from 4 a.m. to 4 a.m. the next day. We use TUACTDUR24, which truncates the final activity at that boundary. A stretch at either edge may continue outside the observed day; we do not join opposite edges. The raw stop time extends past 4 a.m. in 6,787 diaries. Displayed end times are clipped consistently to the diary day.

    All 7,669 records and 139,535 episodes are retained. All sum to 1,440 minutes, with sequential start times and no duplicate diary/episode keys. The 1,490 episodes carrying special data codes (78,651 minutes, about 0.7% of recorded time) appear as “Unclassified.” They are not treated as leisure or silently dropped; they break a measured leisure stretch. Such coding gaps can shorten the apparent stretch.

    Childcare is an overlap, not extra hours

    The inspector reports TRTCCTOT_LN: edited minutes of secondary childcare for children under 13 within each activity. This refers to a child being “in your care” while the respondent did something else; it is not a complete record of attention or all simultaneous work. BLS excludes sleep and specified primary childcare activities from secondary childcare calculations. Primary care for household and nonhousehold people remains a separate activity category.

    In the opening A diary, all 120 TV minutes are recorded as secondary childcare. Across the corpus, 604 episodes have a childcare duration shorter than the episode. For these, the inspector reports the number of minutes but does not invent their placement. A dashed overlay spans an episode only when its whole duration is recorded as secondary care. The diary-level allocation flag is shown where relevant; a flagged diary contains one or more imputed childcare values. No Who or roster join is used.

    Population, weights and uncertainty

    The 2024 annual public-use file represents the U.S. civilian noninstitutionalized population age 15 and older. Its recorded diary dates run from January 1 through December 30, 2024, across all twelve months. One respondent contributes one day; it is not a measure of that person’s usual life. We chose 2024 because the 2025 release has no October microdata after the federal shutdown.

    Each percentage is Σ(TUFINLWGT × indicator) / Σ(TUFINLWGT) within the displayed total-leisure range, including both endpoints. Choosing a longest-stretch bar filters only the record list; it does not change the percentage denominator. Searching an ID searches the complete file and leaves the weighted distribution unchanged. All-totals mode includes zero-leisure days. Listed n values are unweighted diary counts. The weights account for the survey’s unequal selection and day-of-week sampling; a list of records does not itself represent population shares.

    These are descriptive weighted distributions. Replicate weights could not be retrieved for this edition, so no confidence intervals, significance tests, demographic comparisons or causal claims are offered. For inference, the BLS method recomputes an estimate with each of 160 final replicate weights and estimates variance as (4/160) × Σ(replica − full-sample estimate)². A small difference between displayed percentages should not be read as an established population difference. Survey nonresponse, recall, reporting detail and activity coding add further limitations.

    Sources, provenance and reuse

    Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2024 ATUS public-use files. The respondent, activity and activity-summary files are linked by TUCASEID. Episode identity is TUCASEID + TUACTIVITY_N. Every per-code duration independently agrees with the activity-summary file, every weight agrees between files, and every secondary-childcare sum agrees with the respondent file.

    The BLS download host returned an automated-access block during preparation. The original BLS-format files were therefore retrieved from the pinned LongDA archive, revision 1365b6a. No benchmark annotations are used. Record counts, fields, internal totals and published aggregate estimates were checked against BLS documentation. We do not claim byte-for-byte verification against a direct BLS download. This page embeds the derived corpus and makes no runtime requests.

    Definitions: 2024 interview dictionary, 2024 activity lexicon, and ATUS User’s Guide, chapter 7. Year choice: BLS shutdown notice. BLS-produced materials are public domain, except previously copyrighted images. No BLS emblem, photographs or third-party artwork is reproduced.

    The opening examples are explicitly selected for contrasting shape among exactly 120-minute leisure days without unclassified time. A is public ID 20240101240005; B is 20240101241579. The code-switch example is 20240101241612. These letters are visual labels, not invented names. No biographies, occupations or identities are inferred.
